steps.text: Ten days before you plan to serve the ice cream, combine the prunes and Armagnac in a covered container. Set aside.

To make the ice cream, remove six prunes from the container. Set aside. Place the remaining prunes and Armagnac in a food processor or blender. Process to a coarse puree. Set aside. Combine the milk with ⅔ cup of the sugar in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Stir to dissolve sugar. Remove from heat. Set aside.

Beat the remaining sugar with the egg yolks until the mixture is pale yellow and thick. Slowly whisk 1 cup of the hot milk mixture into yolks. Pour the hot custard into the saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it reaches 175 degrees on a candy thermometer. Remove the saucepan from the heat. Set aside until cool. Add the prune puree. Refrigerate until chilled. Pour into the bowl of an ice-cream maker and proceed as directed. Scoop the ice cream into individual bowls and garnish with the reserved prunes.

name: Glazed Carrots With Orange and Ginger
author: Mark Bittman
description: When carrots are cooked, it’s often a sad affair. They are boiled to death and presented almost as an apology. Yet when they’re treated with the respect they deserve, even ordinary supermarket carrots can be among the most reliable and enjoyable of vegetables, especially from fall through spring. This braise-and-glaze technique can be varied at will and can also be used with other roots, like beets, turnips and radishes. Once you have the hang of the technique, changing the flavorings is a snap. Try substituting a mixture of half balsamic vinegar, half water or soy sauce similarly diluted for the orange juice, adding a few cloves of peeled garlic with the carrots. Or add a half cup or so of chopped onions, shallots, scallions or leeks, or of chopped pitted dates or raisins, dried currants or even dried tomatoes.

ingredients.raw: 1 pound carrots, trimmed and peeled if necessary, cut into ¼-inch coins or sticks
ingredients.preparation: trimmed and peeled if necessary, cut into ¼-inch coins or sticks

ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons butter or extra virgin olive oil
ingredients.item: butter or extra virgin olive oil

ingredients.raw: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon minced or grated peeled fresh ginger
ingredients.item: minced or grated peeled fresh ginger

ingredients.raw: ⅓ cup freshly squeezed orange juice
Chopped fresh parsley, dill, mint, basil or chervil leaves for garnish (optional)
ingredients.preparation: dill, mint, basil or chervil leaves for garnish

steps.text: Combine all ingredients except lemon juice and garnish in a saucepan no more than 6 inches across. Bring mixture to a boil, stirring to coat, then adjust heat so mixture simmers. Cover.

Cook, more or less undisturbed, until carrots are tender and liquid is almost gone, 10 to 20 minutes. Uncover and boil off remaining liquid, then add lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Serve hot or within an hour or two, garnished with herbs, if you like.

name: Glazed Mango With Sour Cream Sorbet And Black Pepper
author: Alain Ducasse

ingredients.raw: 2 large mangoes, ripe but not soft
4 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus butter for baking sheet

steps.text: Peel mangoes. Cut in thirds horizontally, leaving the pit in middle section. Place each portion without pit cut-side down on a work surface, and with a large knife cut into 8 slices perpendicular to the cutting board. Gently push down on slices so they spread out and overlap slightly.
Sliver enough mango flesh left around the pits to make ½ cup. Set slivers aside.
Butter a baking sheet large enough to hold mangoes in a single layer. Heat the broiler.

Melt remaining butter in a large nonstick skillet. Use a spatula to place each sliced mango third in the pan so they keep their shape. Cook over medium heat about 5 minutes, sprinkling with two tablespoons sugar, and basting with pan juices.
With spatula, transfer mangoes to baking sheet, place under broiler, and broil until edges just start to color. Do not overcook. Set mangoes aside.

Add remaining sugar to juices in skillet, and cook over medium heat until juices start to caramelize. Add lemon juice, and continue to cook, stirring, until amber colored. Season lightly with pepper. Spoon on mangoes.

Place a sliced caramelized mango third in each of 4 shallow soup plates. Spoon passion fruit sauce around each, and scatter raw mango slivers around. Top each with a large oval scoop of sour cream sorbet, sprinkle ¼ teaspoon coarse pepper on top and serve at once.
